comment: The sole miss was B versus D: plain SGD at .0003 beat .001 on the identical GELU/terminal-LN network. I incorrectly converted a 3.33× rate increase into guaranteed improvement. K1003 supported slow SGD relative to adaptive optimizers, not monotonic SGD rate ordering; K1012 warned against treating progress estimates as decisive. K1002/K1004 helped rank E, C and A. Backtesting found one matched univariate history comparison, favoring the higher rate; the lab contained zero exact-model univariate plain-SGD rate pairs. Six architecture-confounded comparisons across six lab sets also favored higher rates. Thus this reversal is instance-specific evidence. Optimization-path or held-out generalization differences are plausible, but ordinal gold does not identify the mechanism or justify a lower-rate rule.
